choiceReviews.rationale: The option expressly freezes the training snapshot and omits later retrieval. Even if that snapshot accurately captured an earlier policy, it cannot supply the records retrieved for this request after policy edits or establish their request-level lineage. The unit distinguishes weight adaptation from supplying current context at inference time.

Reusing one unversioned summary after policy edits does not identify the current records supplied for a later request. A maintained retrieval cache is a different design: the option provides neither refresh/version guarantees nor request-specific record attribution.

General pretrained knowledge does not establish this organization's edited policy rows or which records supplied this request's context. Even a coincidentally correct inferred policy would lack the required retrieval evidence. The source motivates domain-specific retrieval rather than treating model knowledge as an authoritative policy store.

This plan supplies the applicable records at request time, includes them as generation context, and retains identifiers for the records actually supplied. It is the only offered plan addressing both changing knowledge and source lineage without updating weights for each edit. Compliance of the eventual answer still requires application checks.

choiceReviews.rationale: WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPER removes the default row array, while this suffix neither creates items nor includes the NULL Note. The fixed query has two rows, so a single-row unwrapped-object use case cannot justify this suffix for the stated rooted-array contract.

ROOT('items') wraps the default two-element array correctly, but Note for ProductId 17 is omitted because INCLUDE_NULL_VALUES is absent. The receiving contract distinguishes an explicit JSON null from a missing property, so correct nesting alone is insufficient.

INCLUDE_NULL_VALUES preserves Note:null, but WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPER still removes the array and no items root is requested. Correct null representation does not satisfy the other independent structural requirements.

The default array retains both ordered rows, ROOT('items') adds the required outer property, and INCLUDE_NULL_VALUES preserves Note:null for ProductId 17. The logical output is {"items":[{"ProductId":17,"Note":null},{"ProductId":23,"Note":"Restocked"}]}, satisfying every supplied requirement.

The fixture explicitly stays below the bound and uses nvarchar text, so its content string can be decoded before another parse. The SQL Server 2016+/Azure SQL scope concerns this established operation; no native-json RETURNING behavior is needed.

The actual Return value and lax/strict table restrict JSON_QUERY to an object or array at the selected path: a scalar string yields null in lax mode or an error in strict mode. That rules out b on this exact outer content token. The optional WITH ARRAY WRAPPER section requires native json input and does not alter this nvarchar scalar case.

The actual with_clause/AS JSON section requires nvarchar(max) AS JSON for a nested fragment in an explicit typed schema. However, the Arguments default-schema example also returns Array_value as textual ["a","r","r","a","y"] with type 4, and Return value documents the default Value column as nvarchar(max). Thus an ordinary SELECT projection of the default value preserves an array without AS JSON. This is a source-backed counterexample to treating d as unconditionally wrong when the stem never requires WITH.

choiceReviews.rationale: JSON_VALUE can decode the supplied short content string, after which OPENJSON can parse its separate document. In an explicit WITH schema, Answer nvarchar(max) '$.answer' and Citations nvarchar(max) '$.citations' AS JSON preserve the scalar and array. This intended key works, but its validity alone does not establish uniqueness because d leaves the OPENJSON schema unspecified.

At the supplied outer path, content is a JSON string, not an object or array. JSON_QUERY therefore yields null in default lax mode or an error in strict mode instead of decoding that string. Parsing its result cannot recover the intended inner document.

The outer document has no child answer or citations property beneath the scalar content token. Those keys exist only in the JSON text encoded inside the string. Direct outer paths cannot substitute for interpreting that second document.

This is wrong for an explicit WITH column such as Citations nvarchar(max) '$.citations' without AS JSON, but that restriction appears only in the explanation and author claim, not the stem or this option. With the same decoded document, default-schema OPENJSON returns the citations row's value as nvarchar(max) text [17,23] and type 4. Selecting that ordinary value column as Citations, alongside the answer row's value, returns the required outputs without AS JSON. The option is therefore defensible under a legitimate reading and cannot be attested contradicted.
